title: Government plans to register journalists and set education rules
excerpt: A draft Press Council Act amendment would create a register of journalists and let the council fine media for ethical breaches.

image.alt: The National Press Club building in Dhaka
image.credit: Nurunnaby Chowdhury (Hasive) / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

content:
The government has drafted changes to the Press Council Act 1974 that would make the Press Council register journalists and set minimum educational qualifications for them, Information Minister Andaleeve Rahman told Parliament on Thursday, 12 November, The Daily Star reported.

What the draft would do

  • Register: the Press Council would register journalists, much as the Bar Council does for lawyers, and keep an online database of recognised journalists.
  • Education: minimum qualifications for journalists. The level was not given.
  • Fines: editors, publishers and journalists who break the code of conduct by publishing false, harassing or unethical reports could be fined. No amounts were given.
  • Investigations: the council could act against outlets and journalists for ethical breaches, harming the public interest, or spreading rumours, fake news and hate speech.

Mr Rahman said the changes would make the council "more powerful, effective and media-friendly". State Minister for Information Yasser Khan Choudhury said the government was talking regularly with journalist bodies, including the Dhaka Reporters Unity (DRU), the Bangladesh Federal Union of Journalists (BFUJ) and the Dhaka Union of Journalists (DUJ), and would build the database with them. He also said "it is not appropriate for the government to determine who may enter a profession", according to the newspaper.

The report did not include responses from journalist bodies or rights groups, or a timeline for the bill.

Why it matters

Local journalists, community radio staff and citizen reporters are often the first to expose problems in aid delivery, land, labour and local government. A licensing-style register with fines for "rumours" could shrink the space for that reporting, especially outside Dhaka. Media development NGOs and press freedom groups will want to see the draft text, which comes as the cyber law is also being revised.

What to watch

Publication of the draft amendment, the positions of journalist unions, and whether community and online journalists would need to register.

Sources
